name: National Bolshevism
summary: National Bolshevism is a syncretic current that fuses radical nationalism with Bolshevik-style socialism. Its adherents treat the nation as the highest value, want a revolution that nationalises industry and land under a planned economy, and look to Soviet Russia as an ally against the liberal, capitalist West and the Versailles order. Strands differ over democracy, race and religion.
scope: Weimar-era German National Bolshevism as set out in Karl Otto Paetel's 1933 manifesto for the Group of Social-Revolutionary Nationalists, with Ernst Niekisch's Widerstand circle and the Laufenberg-Wolffheim Hamburg group as its relatives. The 1990s-2000s Russian National Bolshevik Party of Limonov and Dugin is used only where it echoes the same positions. Excludes Strasserism, Ustryalov's Smena Vekh and later Western internet NazBol groups.

notes: The German strand used here is anti-Nazi and anti-fascist in its own words but is Volkisch, with a neo-pagan religious wing; Niekisch's circle was more authoritarian and Prussian-minded. The 1994 Russian programme was openly illiberal and total-statist, and was moderated to a liberal 'minimum programme' in 2004 (s3), so many answers differ by strand. The Russian party's definition of nation was cultural, not racial. Later pass 2026-11-12 (rules 7): the answers that rested on Wikipedia (s2, s4), on the Russian National Bolshevik Party's programmes (s3; a party, outside the scope above) or on a split between strands were nulled, leaving the Paetel manifesto (s1) as the main evidence for the German strand. Themes searched in the manifesto text: economy and property, state and councils, foreign policy and Versailles, religion, race and the Volk, the peasantry, war and force. The manifesto is silent on most of the bank's themes (gender, criminal justice, technology, ecology, immigration, social policy), so those stay null.
